title: Filolial 49
paragraphs: “This sounds kind of tough… Are you okay?”
“It’s just a busy time right now. There must be situations where we can’t just keep Naofumi at Shieldfreeden all the time.”
“Well… I guess so.”

…She has a point. Normally, the Shieldfreeden lot are the kind of people who’d be done with a job as soon as they get paid. However, for various reasons, there are things that simply have to be done at Shieldfreeden. We need to resolve this issue as quickly as possible so we can wipe out the remaining Takt forces, capture the Trash, and deal with the waves.

“Above all, it’s fine now. If those Takt women show up, we’ll take them alive. Even if Gaelion doesn’t come back, I’ll periodically back him up with the Spear Hero’s spear, so if you place a dragon egg nearby, he’ll be revived.”
“No, I don’t think that’s really okay…”
“Are you worried about me?”
Rival, seizing the moment, gives him a sultry look and rests her hand on Father’s chin.
“Eh… no, I mean, when someone tells me it’s fine even if I die, I can’t just say, ‘Oh, okay.’”
“Father! Rival is trying to seduce you! You’ve got to be careful!”
“Boo!”
In response to my protest, Father turns toward me, squinting slightly and letting out a faint sigh. But this is a perfectly reasonable point, after all.
“Listen, Motoyasu… what’s the point of making such a fuss over something like this?”
“But!”
“Anyway, since we’re all set, let’s head to Shieldfreeden.”
“It’s Gaelion’s debut.”
Guh… Why on earth do I have to bring Rival along for the sake of this incredibly troublesome country!? It’s all because Shieldfreeden worships dragons, you know. …Is it wrong to worship dragons?
“I’m going to spread the Church of Filolial-sama in Shieldfreeden all on my own! Sakura-chan! We’re going the idol route!”
“Idols, you say… Well, if it goes well, we might be able to give them a run for their money.”

Just like in the first world, where Filo became an idol and united the world, I’m counting on Sakura-chan and the others to do their best! Sakura-chan is just like Filo-tan. There’s no doubt she can do the same thing.
“Don’t worry. I’m Member No. 00 of the Filo-tan Fan Club, and I’ve got a thing or two to say about Idols.”
“Huh? Motoyasu-kun, you’re an Idol otaku?”
“No, that’s not it. I’m a Filo-tan otaku.”
“O-oh, I see…”
In that case, it might be a good idea to bring in my Finacée—who was quite capable as a manager—to help out. But it’s doubtful my Finacée would actually come all the way to Shieldfreeden.
By the way, while Sakura-chan was spending a week training Rival, she was having a great time hanging out with her Finacée in Melromarc. It seems they’ve already made plans to hang out again.
“Huh? Sakura, an Idol? What’s an Idol?”
Sakura-chan replied in her usual laid-back tone.
“An Idol is an Idol.”
“An Idol…”
“That’s right. An Idol.”
“Idol—”
Sakura-chan answered in a laid-back manner. She was flapping her hands back and forth—it was adorable. With this, maybe she’ll be able to pull it off?
“That’s not really an explanation… Um, to put it simply, it’s a job where you dance and sing cutely in front of everyone, I guess.”
“Huh? Is that fun?”
“Of course! It’s all glitz and glamour!”
“Glitz and glamour? Hmm?”
Ugh… Sakura-chan just isn’t getting the appeal of being an Idol. With her looks, becoming a popular Idol shouldn’t be a pipe dream.
“Sakura-chan is so laid-back… it might be hard for her to be an Idol.”
“She can do it!”

If Filo-tan can do it, Sakura-chan can too! But… it’s true that Sakura-chan is a laid-back Filolial-sama. It’s hard to imagine her dancing and singing with such agility. I wonder if she can adopt an Idol’s perspective… We’ll have to practice that.
In that case, Yuki-chan should debut with us too! Let’s form a unit! Double the impact! Yuki-chan’s crest feathers are twitching as she listens quietly, so she must not mind!
“Yuki-chan too, you know.”
“Understood!”

Yuki-chan responded with great enthusiasm. If we leave it to the leadership-minded Yuki-chan, she might take a Rival route to hype up Filo-tan, just like the Ku-s from the First World did. With Sakura-chan and Yuki-chan, they won’t overshadow each other’s personalities.
I can see it… I can really see it. Gentle, soft-spoken Sakura-chan and Yuki-chan, with her crisp, crystal-clear voice, standing on stage in dazzling costumes… This is definitely going to work!
“What about Kou?”
“Can Kou wear an Idol outfit?　I think his outfit would be a flashier version of the dresses Yuki-chan and the others are wearing… Well, maybe it’d work if we go with a boy Idol concept?”
“Eh…”

Kou’s furrowing his brows. Midori was happy to wear it, but Kou seems to hate the idea. But don’t worry. With the money we earn from our idol activities, we’ll let Kou eat as much of his favorite food as he wants.

“We’ll mobilize all the Filolial-sama and go the idol route! My first Father sold merchandise that came with perks like handshake opportunities! Let’s take that as a model and sell our way through sheer numbers of Filolial-sama.”

Heh heh heh… Rival, you’re just one person after all, but we have countless Filolial-sama on our side. If we travel around Shieldfreeden together to maintain public order and boost food supply and demand, while simultaneously running the business that Father taught me, the Dragon Cult will fade away easily. Plus, we can use a human wave tactic to flush out the Takt faction. It’s killing two birds with one stone.
“Filolial 49… is that what it’ll be like?”
“What’s that supposed to mean?”

“It’s the name of an idol group with a lot of members. In my world, there’s an idol famous for business tactics like handshake events. Everyone has their own tastes, after all. When there are so many of them, you’re bound to find an idol you really root for.”
Oh! That’s great! It’s perfect for Filolial-sama, who loves competing for speed.

Hmm? That reminds me of an incident I had with a pig who used to dream of becoming an idol. I recall meeting a few of them. There were pigs who gave up their dreams as soon as I threw some sweet words their way, pigs who worked even harder and became Idols… and even pigs who ventured overseas. Anyway, if I use my own unique presentation ideas like I did back then, I’m sure it’ll work out just fine!
“Do your best for Naofumi!”
Muuu! That’s right! Someday I’ll make you eat your words!
“No matter what the situation, as long as Lord Kitamura remains steadfast like that, I’m starting to think things will work out somehow.”
“Aren’t you just resigning yourself to defeat?”
“I think so too.”

Éclair and the others were saying things like that, but I’m ignoring them! It’ll take a little time to mobilize all of Filolial-sama’s forces, but we’ll make up for lost ground in no time! And so, we headed to Shieldfreeden to unveil our Rival.

So, having brought our Rival to Shieldfreeden, we summoned the city’s leadership and held a presentation for him. The councilor who had proposed that Father should command dragons was the first to arrive, rushing in to bow to Father at the meeting and take his seat. Gradually, the council members began gathering.
“Well then… based on the wishes of the Shield Heroes, I intend to restart the reforms of Shieldfreeden,”
the meeting began with those words.
“Shield Hero. I hear you’ve raised a dragon as proposed…”

The councilor who had proposed raising the dragon raised his hand, and after receiving approval, stood up to ask. Then Father nodded, but before he could answer, Rival raised his hand. That was a remarkably well-timed reaction.
“That’s me, Gaelion. I came here exactly as you proposed.”
While some council members looked on skeptically, the council member who had made the proposal nodded firmly.
“Takt’s dragon has often taken human form as well. Therefore, Gaelion, would you mind providing some proof that you are indeed a dragon?”
“Of course. Besides, it’s already been decided that I’ll give a presentation once this discussion is over.”
Rival stood up and—flap!—spread his dragon wings to assert himself.
“I can’t be lumped in with small fry like Takt’s dragon. But pulling a stunt like this is a piece of cake for me.”
As if to show off, Rival instantly transformed into a baby dragon and hovered above the conference room table. The councilor standing behind the one who made the proposal lets out a startled gasp.
What’s that about? Did Father really think he could show off by claiming he couldn’t recreate the dragon Takt used to keep? Too bad—Rival is actually a much trickier opponent than Takt’s dragon.
“I certainly understand. However, I wouldn’t exactly recommend taking on such a fragile form, would I?”
“I suppose there’s also the strategy of lulling the opponent into a false sense of security… After all…”

While still hovering in midair, Rival closes his eyes for a moment, then glares intently at the assembly members. Ah, he’s radiating a certain killing intent. It has that unique aura characteristic of monsters.
“Guh…”
“Ugh…”

Struck by the killing intent Rival emitted, some of the council members began to groan. Quite a few of them turned pale. To be flustered by killing intent of this magnitude—it really shows their true caliber.
“Don’t underestimate a dragon… A true champion isn’t just one who puts on a brave front.”

His previous fawning tone faded away, and Rival responded in a tone reminiscent of a parent. Though even that parent is a pathetic dragon, isn’t he? HAHAHA, it’s no use for a pathetic parent and child to try to act cool, is it?
“I’ll show my true form when the time is right. Is that acceptable?”

“Yes. If you can project that level of intimidation, I believe you’ll fully meet our expectations and live up to the faith of Shieldfreeden. We’ll lend our support, but please understand that this will be a long battle.”
The councilor who made the proposal replied without so much as a flicker of emotion.
“The human world is such a hassle.”
Putting aside his killing intent and letting out a slight sigh, Rival returned to human form and took his seat.
“If you’re not satisfied, I’ll take you on anytime. Come at me.”

Rival is beckoning me with a few casual gestures, as if to show how relaxed he is. He’s completely getting carried away. Do you really think you’ve become the champion just from spending a week hunting at sea with Father-in-law?

Father-in-law is the strongest! Next come me, Filo-tan, and my older sister. After that come Filolial-sama and the others—at best, you’ll be on the same level once Ren and Itsuki have been properly strengthened! Ugh… If Father weren’t watching me, I’d have to call him out on this.
“Then… may I request a grand presentation to the people this afternoon, here in the capital of Shieldfreeden?”
“Of course. Let’s show them the divinity of Gaelion.”
“Thank you for your cooperation.”

And so, the meeting proceeded in an orderly fashion. As for the reforms we discussed last time, the consensus was that we couldn’t do anything without first gaining the people’s support. However, it seems the councilor who proposed the reforms had been laying the groundwork behind the scenes, and progress is reportedly being made on resolving the issue of vested interests—which had been a minor sticking point?

Incidentally, the presence of rivals caused such intense anxiety that several lawmakers fell ill during the meeting and had to leave their seats. Isn’t that a bit pathetic? Eventually, once the meeting had reached a natural break… presumably because preparations were complete, we moved outside the Shieldfreeden building.
“Whoa… there’s a huge gathering here.”

Looking outside the building, I could see a large crowd gathered beyond the iron fence. It felt like the scene in Japan when a massive crowd gathers in front of the National Diet Building. I don’t quite remember what the situation was like back then.

Ah, but I seem to recall that when I went abroad a long time ago, a pig who was acting like a princess gathered people like this to unite the country. …Come to think of it, I’ve actually encountered pigs who called themselves princesses a few times. I’d completely forgotten about that. Well, it’s a memory that doesn’t really matter.
“So, this is where Gaelion’s debut takes place.”
“Gaelion-chan, be careful.”
“I’ll be fine!”

And so, we stepped out into the garden with its great view and slowly walked up to the stage. Then Father and Rival took the stage… and stood in front of the seats, ready to give a grand presentation. I watched Rival, who was getting a bit too full of himself, along with Sakura-chan and Filolial-sama, all of us gritting our teeth as we observed the scene.

“I am Naofumi Iwatani, the Shield Hero, here on an inspection visit from Siltvelt. People of Shieldfreeden. Over the past two weeks, I’ve had the opportunity to observe various aspects of your country’s internal affairs. And… to demonstrate here exactly what your country expects from the Shield Hero, and what I have been lacking… that is why I have arranged this gathering.”
With that, Father paused for a moment before turning his gaze toward Rival. As always, Rival is exuding an air of a champion.
Don’t let him fool you, everyone!
